summary.headline: Wonderla Q4 FY26 revenue rose 40% YoY to INR135 crore and EBITDA doubled to INR43.8 crore at 32% margin, helped by Chennai ramp-up and a Labour Code provision reversal.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever Q4 by income, with revenue from operations up 40% YoY to INR135 crore and footfalls up 30% to 8.79 lakh, driven mainly by the newly opened Chennai park. PAT rose 49% to INR16.4 crore, aided by reversal of certain tax and Labour Code-related provisions created in Q3 FY26. For full FY26, revenue grew 13% to INR518.8 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to INR160 crore, but PAT fell 25% to INR81.7 crore against a deferred-tax credit of INR24.1 crore in FY25. Hyderabad footfall declined 7% for the year, and management guided to no large capex in FY27 apart from sustaining capex of INR35-40 crore.

financial_highlights.change: -25% YoY (vs INR109.3 crore; FY25 included INR24.1 crore deferred tax credit)

segments.name: Chennai Park (commenced Dec 2025)
segments.commentary: December footfall about 75,000 at launch; Q4 footfall about 1.91 lakh per management's figure cited by analyst. Management says first full quarter performance is in line with mature Kochi and Hyderabad parks, with Q4 EBITDA margin about 30%.

segments.name: Hyderabad Park
segments.commentary: FY26 footfall down about 7% YoY, attributed to summer weather and early monsoon, a school-group ban after road incidents (est. 50,000-60,000 footfall impact), and softer Q3 school groups. Management says it is still strong on a two-year basis.

segments.name: Bhubaneswar Park
segments.commentary: Close to 2 lakh footfall in FY26, first full year. Target about 2.5 lakh in FY27 (about 20% growth), with mid-term potential of 3-3.2 lakh.

segments.name: Resort and Hospitality
segments.commentary: Best-ever performance in Q4 on strong demand and occupancy. ISLE gaming pod commenced operations in June 2025 per management; current ADR about INR6,300, with 7-12% ADR uplift expected after Bangalore resort refurbishment.

guidance_outlook: No large capex planned in FY27; sustaining capex of about INR35-40 crore.
Incremental depreciation from Chennai about INR45-50 crore annualised in FY27 (about INR13 crore booked for four months); overall depreciation about INR80-83 crore per quarter currently.
Management expects EBITDA margins to settle around 40% over the next year as launch costs fade, subject to all parks including Chennai delivering.
A&P spend to be maintained at 7-8% of top line; no launch expenses expected in Q1 FY27.
Management aims to add at least 5 more parks, with 2-3 of the next 5 likely done within about 5 years; expects to close 1-2 real estate deals in FY27 across about 4 state governments.
Management says non-ticket revenue share should move towards 50:50 within 4-5 years, with 40:60 near term.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex: no large projects; sustaining capex INR35-40 crore.
CWIP of INR102.9 crore relates to Sky Wheel at Chennai, new attractions and a Bangalore roller coaster; to be capitalised in Q1 FY27.
Chennai park mature in about 3-4 years; management sees Chennai and Bangalore as top revenue parks long-term, followed by Hyderabad and Kochi.
Focus on Tier 1 cities over Tier 2 for new parks; Tier 1 land acquisition and state approvals are slower. Asset-light models being explored in larger cities.
Gross investment in assets about INR1,000-1,200 crore per management.
demand_pricing: Q1 FY27 trading: Chennai doing very well; some other parks growing, others flat; heat wave has not caused much damage so far.
West Asia tensions noted as a possible supply-chain and discretionary spend risk for April-May.
Management says Chennai is in a category already created by existing water parks, making market entry easier.
Hyderabad softness linked to weather and school-group ban; Ramoji Film City cited as a non-competing film city.
Management guides against predicting footfall or EBITDA until a full year at Chennai is complete.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Chennai footfall moderate to about 64,000 per month after strong December start, and what is happening in Hyderabad (FY26 footfall down 7%)?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai: December launch month had higher marketing spend and Christmas seasonality; Jan-Feb are lean months. Hyderabad: early monsoon, Operation Sindoor-linked demand softness in summer 2025, and school-group weakness in Q3; management says two-year growth is still strong.

qa_highlights.question: Why are FY26 EBITDA margins only about 30% when older parks run around 40%?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO: corporate cost centre, one-time Labour Code costs, ESOP expenses, Chennai launch expenses and corporate setup costs are absorbed into the parks' margins.

qa_highlights.question: Why has the QIP-funded expansion been slow, and what is the status of new deals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says the shift to Tier 1 cities (land scarcity, slower government approvals) is the only cause; it is in talks with at least 4 state governments and hopes to close 1-2 deals this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for depreciation and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Chennai adds about INR45-50 crore annual depreciation; new investments add 8-10% of cost to annual depreciation. Margins expected to normalise towards 40% as parks mature.

qa_highlights.question: Will Bangalore resort ADR move after refurbishment?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO expects a 7-12% ADR increase from the current about INR6,300 after the refurbishment.

qa_highlights.question: Why do new rides not drive repeat visits?
qa_highlights.answer: MD: day outings need planning and most guests visit once a year or less; repeat rates are structurally low, and the core target is the 10-25 age group.

risks_watch: Hyderabad footfall trend: second consecutive year of decline, with FY26 footfall down about 7%.
Chennai sustainability: management declines to forecast beyond one full year; Q4 Chennai footfall moderated from the December launch peak.
Discretionary spend and West Asia tensions could pressure FY27 demand and supply chains.
Pace of new park additions: depends on Tier 1 land and state approvals; no deal signed yet.
Depreciation step-up of about INR45-50 crore in FY27 from Chennai, plus launch-cost normalisation to test margin recovery.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth and Chennai, but cautious on near-term visibility; management repeatedly declined to give footfall, EBITDA or deal-timing forecasts, citing uncertainty and variability.
key_quotes: During this quarter, we had our highest ever Q4 with an income growing by 32% Y-o-Y, about INR142 crores, supported by footfalls of roughly INR8.79 lakhs.
We don't know EBITDA. 30% is the EBITDA margin for the last quarter.
We are at least talking to at least 4 state governments at any given point in time.
Near term, it will be 40-60 only. But definitely, I think in the next 4, 5 years, it should move to the 50-50 mark.

adds.what: Sky Wheel, new attractions and Bangalore roller coaster (CWIP INR102.9 crore) to be capitalised; no new park commissioned in call

growth.why: No explicit FY27 revenue growth guidance; management guides against predicting footfall or EBITDA until a full Chennai year, with Chennai ramp, Bhubaneswar target of 2.5 lakh (~20%), and ADR uplift of 7-12% at Bangalore as partial support, and no large capex planned in FY27 beyond INR35-40 crore sustaining capex.
